notes: Thai hotel booking confirmation of a fictional hotel, 1 page, Leelawadee UI. Thai is written without spaces between words: a line wrapped inside a sentence joins with NO space. Thai sentences carry no final punctuation; in the source each sentence is separated from the next by one space, and each key sentence is one such unit. Dates are in the Buddhist era (2569 = 2026). The dark band at the top (hotel name, address line, contact line) is a letterhead: furniture. The booking number and issue date line, the salutation "เรียน ..." and the closing "ขอแสดงความนับถือ / ฝ่ายสำรองห้องพัก" are body metadata, not sentences. Two boxes sit SIDE BY SIDE (guest data left, stay details right), read box by box, left box first; each holds a key/value table without header row, and the box labels are labels, not headings. In the charges table the summary rows ("รวม" ... "ยอดคงเหลือ...") have a label spanning the first three columns, so the label repeats in those three grid cells. The cancellation list uses TYPED Thai-digit markers "๑." "๒." "๓." set apart by a hanging indent. The "included" list uses CSS "thai" markers, which LOOK the same (๑. ๒. ...) but are not in the text. The two last sections sit side by side as two columns: the left section (heading and its list) is read before the right one.
